Absolutely! Here’s a detailed 7-day Armenia adventure itinerary that blends hiking, adventure, culture, food, wine, and authentic local experiences. All information is based on official tourism sources and the most current travel blogs/websites retrieved above.

7-Day Adventure Itinerary: Armenia
Logistics & General Notes
Best travel window: April–November (good weather for hiking and festivals)
Base city: Yerevan (well-connected and central for day-trips/overnights)
Bring modest clothes for churches, sturdy footwear for hiking, and expect meal costs: Budget ($8–15), Mid-range ($20–35); vegetarian and halal options widely available
Day 1: Yerevan – Arrival & Culinary Welcome

Morning:

Arrive at Zvartnots International Airport, Yerevan. Transfer to hotel and check-in.
Leisure stroll in city center: Republic Square, attend singing fountain show (seasonal evenings).

Afternoon:

Food intro: Lunch at Lavash Restaurant (Armenian specialties like dolma and khorovats).
Visit GUM Market: Taste fresh apricots, local cheese, churchkhela (walnut/candy).

Evening:

Optional dinner at Dolmama (highly rated for traditional and modern Armenian cuisine).
Overnight in Yerevan.
Day 2: Hiking & Heritage – Garni Gorge, Geghard, & Lavash Experience

Morning:

Early transfer to Garni Temple (Greco-Roman, 77 AD; Entry: 1,500 AMD).
Hike the Garni Gorge: Marvel at “Symphony of Stones” basalt columns (~1.5-2h easy hike).
Practical: Modest dress. Bring water/snacks for hike.

Afternoon:

Visit Geghard Monastery (UNESCO, carved into mountain; free entry). Photograph acoustics and khachkars.
Lunch/Experience: Lavash bread baking in a nearby village home (includes meal and workshop).

Evening:

Return to Yerevan (~40min drive).
Stroll Vernissage Market (traditional crafts, local sweets).
Overnight in Yerevan.
Day 3: South Armenia – Adventure & Monasteries (Khor Virap & Noravank)

Morning:

Depart to Khor Virap Monastery (Mt. Ararat views, historic prison site; 30km from Yerevan).
Hike short trails around the monastery for panoramic photos.

Afternoon:

Continue to Noravank Monastery (dramatic red rock canyon, unique two-story Surb Astvatsatsin church).
Stop for lunch: Try khorovats (Armenian BBQ) at a local guesthouse.
Visit Areni region: Explore cave winery archaeological site and Areni Wine Factory (wine tasting of Areni Noir).

Evening:

Dinner at a village guesthouse, optional home-cooked meal or wine-country restaurant.
Overnight in or near Areni (guesthouse or small hotel – rural Armenia experience).
Day 4: Tatev Monastery & The Wings of Tatev (Adventure Day)

Morning:

Early drive to Halidzor (for Tatev cable car; ~2 hrs from Areni).
Ride the Wings of Tatev – world’s longest reversible cable car (5.7km; 5,000 AMD return).
Visit Tatev Monastery (medieval university, spectacular clifftop views).

Afternoon:

Optional nearby hikes along the Vorotan River gorge.
Lunch: Try harissa at a local restaurant (ancient wheat & meat dish).

Evening:

Return towards Yerevan (stop midway for dinner), or overnight in Goris for added adventure (visit Old Goris for traditional meal at Mirhav Restaurant).
Day 5: Vayots Dzor Wine Touring & Outdoor Exploration

Morning:

Guided wine tour through Vayots Dzor Province (visit Zorah, Kataro, Voskevaz, with tasting and cave cellars).
Walking between some vineyards (light hiking option available).

Afternoon:

Lunch at Trinity Canyon Vineyards or similar.
Optional: Village experience or cheese-making in Areni.
Return to Yerevan by evening.

Evening:

Dinner at Pandok Yerevan (try khash if available; typical winter specialty).
Day 6: Lake Sevan & Dilijan National Park (Nature & Relaxation)

Morning:

Day trip to Lake Sevan (Armenia’s largest lake).
Visit Sevanavank Monastery; hike the peninsula or along the shoreline.

Afternoon:

Continue to Dilijan National Park (called "Armenian Switzerland") for light hiking on the Parz Lake trail, or just enjoy lakefront cafés.
Lunch: Haykanoush Restaurant (try trout or local vegetarian
